yt_title: How does a microwave actually heat food? #shorts
yt_description: Build a microwave from scratch and see how it really works. #science #howitworks #microwave #shorts

scenes.text: Your leftovers are ice cold, and you want them hot in two minutes. So let's build a microwave.
Food is full of water. And every water molecule is like a tiny magnet, with a plus side and a minus side.
Hit them with an electric field, and they all spin to line up with it. Flip the field, and they flip too.
Now flip it two point four five billion times a second. All that spinning and bumping turns into heat.
To make waves that fast, you need a magnetron. It's a vacuum tube that turns electricity into microwaves.
Fire them into a metal box. Metal reflects microwaves, so they bounce around inside, and can't get out.
But you want to see your food. So the window gets a metal mesh with tiny holes. Light fits through. The twelve centimeter waves don't.
One problem. The waves pile up into hot spots and cold spots. One bite is lava, the next is still frozen.
So you add a spinning plate, to move your food through the hot spots and even it out.
Ding. Congratulations. You built a microwave.
And the real one? It was discovered by accident in the nineteen forties, when an engineer's chocolate bar melted in his pocket.
